rules.message: This file was encrypted and is now plaintext. Treat every value in it as exposed: rotate the secrets, then restore encryption before merging.

rules.messageTemplate: {path} was an encrypted value and is now stored in the clear. Rotate it and re-encrypt the file.
A decryption recipient was added at {path}. That key can now decrypt this file — confirm it is authorized and that the change was intended.
A decryption recipient was removed at {path}. Anything that key already read stays readable to its holder — rotate the secrets if the removal was a revocation.

rules.message: The SOPS MAC changed but no value it covers did. A normal edit moves both together, so this points at a hand-edited or tampered metadata block.
This file is now encrypted. Confirm the values it held while plaintext were rotated — git history still has them.

rules.messageTemplate: A SOPS creation rule changed at {path}. This decides who future encryptions are readable by; existing files keep their current recipients until they are re-encrypted.
